doc.title: Gerald Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Detroit's integrated schools and freedom
summary: Wilson recalls Sy Oliver in Detroit and how Detroit had no segregated schools and many freedoms for Black people.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: He went on – he was going to – to join Tommy Dorsey. So Sy, who was my dear friend when I was in school in Detroit, and I see in Detroit all the kids that I ran around with, we were all musicians going to Cass – we were at all of the dances that all of the big bands played. Another thing about Detroit, Michigan which makes it so valuable, you see in Detroit, Michigan, there were no segregated schools in Detroit, Michigan when I went there. And there were people who had graduated years before I got there, so they had never had any segregated schools in

Detroit. There were so many places for freedom for blacks in Detroit. They could go to all the big theaters downtown, they could go to Belle Isle, one of the finest parks in Detroit. It’s still there, you can just look right across the river into Windsor, Canada. So, anyway, the thing about Detroit was good for me and um, the school I went to was good for me because um, they taught so well and they were second only to Julliard.
